value.rationale: Natural incidence hypergraphs of all equal-length sliding windows are standard models of cyclic observational data. Exact concept counts measure closure-representation complexity, with a sharp small-window formula and an exponential fixed-defect regime. The concept count uniquely reconstructs the window width; height and modularity are completely classified for the entire two-parameter family. These motivated full-family invariants go beyond tabulating arbitrary finite slices; no application to arbitrary circular-arc hypergraphs is asserted.
